parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction, so extrapolation runs from structural signals. Positives: no criminalisation of same-sex conduct (since 1993), no trans-specific offence, no facility/border/screening rule documented, no organised targeting, a 2014 statute covering SOGI victims, and reporting that society is relatively tolerant of same-sex conduct with no official service discrimination recorded. Negatives: no trans framework at all, no anti-discrimination recourse, dated (2011-2012) and conflicting stigma/violence evidence, a 2018 NGO statement of some identity-based violence with absent protections, no documented acceptance of gender diversity as such, and weak rule of law (coup, torture, impunity) making any remedy unreliable. No tier-1 or tier-2 exposure appears; worst feature is tier-3 societal stigma with thin recourse. Neither documented acceptance nor documented trans-specific harm carries the weight, leaving mid-scale.
